$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

- **`chat-interpretation-pipeline.ts`** — Remove unreachable `try/catch` around `JSON.parse(extracted)`. `extractSingleJsonObject` already calls `JSON.parse` internally and only returns non-null on success, so the catch branch can never execute. Collapses 7 lines to 1.
- **`http-resilience.ts`** — Throw `RangeError` instead of base `Error` for out-of-range `maxAttempts`/`baseDelayMs` params; `RangeError` is the semantically correct error class for numeric range violations. Also replaces both `Math.pow(2, attempt - 1)` calls with the ES2016 `**` exponentiation operator.
- **`text-model.ts`** — Simplify `trimmedModel && trimmedModel.length > 0 ? trimmedModel : DEFAULT_TEXT_MODEL` to `trimmedModel || DEFAULT_TEXT_MODEL`. A truthy string is already non-empty, so the `.length > 0` guard is redundant.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [x] `npm test` — 416 passed, 1 skipped (same as baseline)

EOF

## Summary by Sourcery

Tighten small core behaviors and clean up minor logic in chat interpretation, HTTP retry handling, and text-model selection.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure HTTP retry options validate numeric ranges using RangeError for invalid maxAttempts and baseDelayMs values.

Enhancements:
- Remove unreachable JSON parse error handling in the chat interpretation pipeline to rely directly on schema parsing.
- Use the exponentiation operator for exponential backoff calculations in HTTP retry logic.
- Simplify text model selection by relying on string truthiness instead of redundant length checks.

## Code Review

This pull request simplifies the chat interpretation pipeline by removing explicit JSON parsing error handling, refactors HTTP resilience utilities to use `RangeError` and the exponentiation operator (`**`), and simplifies the default text model selection logic. The reviewer pointed out that the exponential backoff delays in the HTTP resilience logic are uncapped, which could lead to excessively long wait times or integer overflow in `setTimeout`. It is recommended to cap these delays using `MAX_RETRY_AFTER_MS`.
